evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The Kauai Railway is a former narrow gauge railway company in Hawaii, United States.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: It was created 1906 and operated a 30 km long railroad line with narrow gauge track from Port Allen,to Koloa and Kalaheo on the south coast of the island of Kauai.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: It did not have a connection to the other common carrier railway on the island, the Ahukini Terminal and Railway, although both were built to the same track gauge.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: Almost all railway trackage on Kauai was connected together due to an agreement with the U.S. Government to interconnect the common carriers and sugarcane plantation railways.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The government imposed this as a condition before they would agree to improve the port of Nawiliwili for oceangoing ships.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The line was opened 1907.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: In 1936 the company name was changed to the Kauai Terminal Company.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The last train ran 1947, with rail operations replaced by trucks.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The company continues to exist as the present-day Kauai Commercial Company.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: Incorporated on April 17, 1886, at Marblehead, Ohio, the Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad (L&M) was a short standard gauge railroad that spanned about seven miles (11.3 km) in length.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: It extended from Marblehead through Lakeside to a connection with the Lake Shore and Michigan Southern Railway (later the New York Central Railroad) at Danbury (an unincorporated hamlet bordering Sandusky Bay).

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: A common carrier, it carried both freight and passengers.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: It was abandoned as a common carrier railroad July 31, 1964, operated for the last time as a private industrial railroad in Summer 1978, and its tracks were removed in Fall 1997.
